title: Setup and Seating
section: The Four Winds Around Your Table
text:
The Four Winds Around Your Table
American Mahjong is played by four players, each representing one of the cardinal wind directions.
East - The dealer and starting position
South - Sits to East’s right
West - Sits across from East
North - Sits to East’s left
Fun Fact: The wind seating doesn’t follow a traditional compass layout. In mahjong, the winds follow Asian cardinal points and have traditional associations with seasons (East/Spring, South/Summer, West/Autumn, North/Winter), which may explain why the arrangement differs from a standard compass.














The wind positions rotate throughout the game, giving each player a turn as the dealer. Don’t worry about memorizing everything now, we’ll cover the significance of these positions as we progress through the lessons.

title: The Charleston
text:
After the tiles are dealt, the game begins with a pass called the Charleston. Here, each player passes 3 tiles at a time to other players. A Charleston consists of 3 passes. On the last pass, you can do what is called a blind pass. This means that instead of choosing 3 of your tiles to pass you can choose 0, 1, or 2, and complete the set of three by passing what you were given (without looking). If all players agree, you can do two Charlestons prior to the start of the game. At the end of the Charleston you can also do a courtesy pass of up to 3 tiles with the player across from you. You and the player agree on how many you would like to pass, it is fine to pass 0 if you do not want to pass any more. Let’s practice!


Practice the Charleston:
Select 3 tiles to pass each time. Drag the tiles to the correct player.
First Charleston: Right → Across → Left
Second Charleston: Left → Across → Right
Blind passes can be made on the 2nd Left and 2rd Right.
